text: Türksat 2A, also known as Eurasiasat 1, was a Turkish communications satellite developed as part of a project to establish an immediate network with two geosynchronous satellites, overseen by Türksat A.Ş. in Turkey and Eurasiasat SAM in Monaco. Launched on January 10, 2001, at 21:39 UTC by Arianespace using an Ariane-44P H10-3 launch vehicle from ELA-2 at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, French Guiana, the satellite was successfully inserted into geostationary transfer orbit and subsequently positioned at 42°E, aligning with Türksat 1C, which was launched in 1996. Broadcast services began on February 1, 2001. The satellite was designed to cover Europe, Turkey on the west spot, and Turkey, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Russia on the east spot, enabling simultaneous coverage and direct connectivity between Europe and Central Asia. It is based on the Alcatel Spacebus 3000B3 series, with an on-orbit mass of 3,530 kg (7,780 lb) and 9,200 W of power. Its communications payload includes 36 Ku band transponders: 22 fixed-beam transponders with 33 MHz bandwidth and 10 transponders with 36 MHz bandwidth, plus two additional steerable beams.
